Ratz Instagib 2.0 is a great rail-gun/instagib deathmatch arena-shooter. The aesthetics are visually appealing.

The levels are flooded with monochrome neon with contour lines and shades of grey with relatively flat shading and texture-work. Since you play as rats, the levels are scaled accordingly, which is always a fun gimmick. The color saturation and many other effects can be tweaked to the user's preference or to improve visibility. The maps all work well and have unique designs. The soundtrack is oddly relaxing and energetic, it really adds to the atmosphere.

There's a pseudo rocket-jump mechanic that gives the game a faster pace and higher skill ceiling. The maps are well balanced for 1v1 or more players. The mechanics and netcode are extremely tight and polished, which is exactly what you want from this type of game. You can customize your zoom intensity and independent mouse sensitivity. Flying through maps and flicking shots successfully is very satisfying, but it's a hard-earned skill and is often fleeting. The frustration is mitigated by the fact that the game is build around skill. When you lose, you know it was because you didn't play as well as your opponent(s). The game supports bots, and pretty decent ones at that, which is a godsend because it's not so easy to find populated lobbies anymore.

The only annoyance is that the hitmarker sound occasionally plays when you and your opponent shoot each other at almost the same time, but even plays if the server determines you lost. It's psychologically punishing to my focus to receive false feedback, but is ultimately a mild annoyance that I can accept.

 Overall, I recommend this game pretty strongly for anyone interested in the instagib gamemodes of oldschool FPS games. For $9, it's a no-brainer. The game's very polished, charming and is a lot of fun.

Ratz Instagib is the ultimate high—hands down the best game ever. It’s a relentless, quivering rush of railgun-fueled ecstasy where every shot is a gibbing climax. One flick of the wrist, and BAM—your screen’s drenched in a hot mess of rat bits. These cute little rodents scamper in neon arenas, but it’s all a tease for the main event: unloading a perfect shot that gibs everywhere, leaving you panting. Multiplayer’s a sweaty frenzy of quick, messy gibs. The chiptune beats throb, and that railgun crack—followed by a wet splat—is pure bliss. Every match is a rapid-fire release, coating your monitor in glorious, sticky gib. 11/10—can’t stop gibbing all over this game.
